Hazel eyes are a common occurrence of *central heterochromia*.

Central heterochromia is an eye condition where there are two colors in the same iris; the central (pupillary) zone of the iris is a different color than the mid-peripheral (ciliary) zone, with the true iris color being the outer color.

https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c3/Eye_Central_Heterochromia_crop_and_lighter.jpg

For example, if I had to identify this person's eye color, it's likely I would say "blue and brown," or maybe "blue and gold", although officially they are considered simply "blue".

https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/be/Hazel_Eyes,_Caucasian_Male,_Age_23.jpg

Hazel, in the same vein, is actually "green and brown", or simply "green".
